claims.head: Stay out of the box, Sharks
claims.call: The Oilers’ power play creates at least their usual 9.6 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Sharks’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Oilers’ power play is the best. Discipline matters more than usual for the Sharks tonight. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.

claims.head: Who drives the play: the Oilers
claims.body: At 5-on-5, the Oilers have been near the top of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Sharks one of the worst. The ice should tilt the Oilers’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

notes.text: Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 56% of the team’s power-play time in 4 games, up from 6% last season.

stakes: The Sharks go in tied for third in the Pacific with 6 points, a point behind the Oilers, second. A regulation win for the Sharks would lift them past the Oilers.

SJS.head: A tough matchup for the Sharks
SJS.body: Even though San Jose has home-ice advantage, Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Sharks can pull it off if their power play gets going.

EDM.head: The Oilers have a lot going for them
EDM.body: Even though San Jose has home-ice advantage, Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Sharks can make it interesting if their power play gets going.

story.head: McDavid’s favorite opponent
paras: The Sharks are 3-1-0. The Oilers have won three straight.
The Oilers’ power play has a soft target in the Sharks’ kill. The Oil usually control more of the chances than the Sharks do.

items.text: Darnell Nurse faces Edmonton for the first time since leaving.
Shakir Mukhamadullin faces San Jose for the first time since leaving.
Connor McDavid has a point in nine straight games against San Jose, and 22 points in his last ten against them.
The Oilers are newly without Frederik Andersen, and have had to make do without Zach Hyman, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Matt Savoie all season. Devon Levi is expected to start.
